findings.title: Aurora's aeon act-descriptor exporter emits a struct layout diverged from engine/structs.emp (34B Act vs 40B, 72B Sec vs 66B) and resurrects a directory the engine deleted
findings.claim: generateActDescriptorAsm emits the pre-2026-06 Act/Sec layouts — fields the aeon engine deleted, missing every field it added, and the wrong total sizes — and saveAeonProject writes them into games/sonic4/data/editor/ojz/act1/export/, the exact directory aeon deleted on 2026-08-01 and which sits inside an auto-commit-daemon watch path.
findings.evidence: Aurora emits (act-descriptor.ts:26-40): sec_grid_ptr(4) grid_w(2) grid_h(2) start_local_x(2) start_local_y(2) start_sec_x(1) start_sec_y(1) cam_min_x/cam_max_x/cam_min_y/cam_max_y (8, lines 34-37) act_bg_layout(4) act_bg_tiles(4) act_parallax_config(4) = 34 bytes, and its own comment at :25 says "Act descriptor (34 bytes)". aeon/engine/structs.emp:26-51 declares `Act` as 40 bytes ($28): there is NO cam_min/max block at all, act_bg_layout sits at $0E where Aurora writes cam_min_x, and the engine adds act_art_pool_table($1A), act_art_pool_pages($1E), edge_mode($20), pad_21($21), act_sec_local_maps($22), act_art_budget($26) — none of which Aurora emits. Section side: Aurora emits 14×dc.l + 2×dc.w + 4×dc.b + dc.l + 2×dc.w = 72 bytes/section and pads null sections `dcb.b 72, 0` (act-descriptor.ts:59); aeon/engine/structs.emp:107-132 declares `Sec` as 66 bytes ($42). Field-level: Aurora's `sec_reserved_2C` (:77) is the engine's `sec_block_dict`($2C); Aurora's `sec_collision_s4lz` (:79) was renamed `sec_effects`($34) (aeon docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-14-effects-p3-parcel-c2.md:278); Aurora's `sec_tile_art_s4lz`/`sec_tile_art_vram` (:83-84) no longer exist in the struct; the engine's `sec_camera_lookahead`($3D) and `sec_block_dict_len`($40) are never emitted. Live path: src/core/project/aeon/save.ts:222-243 calls exportAct on every aeon save and writes act_descriptor.asm / entity_data.asm / vram_bases.asm / section_N.*.bin under `${dataPath}export/`. aeon/docs/DEFERRED_WORK.md:988-991 records that commit 46c2e0f (2026-08-01, "Parcel J: delete the parked ojz editor exports") deleted that directory, and DEFERRED_WORK.md:1005 records it "is git-tracked but NOT in the build include graph … it would not even assemble as-is" and "still emits the OLD Act layout: the removed cam_min_x/max_x/min_y/max_y 4-word camera block, no edge_mode byte/pad, and pre-paging art fields". The directory is present on disk again with 2026-08-12 timestamps, i.e. a post-deletion Aurora save recreated it. aeon/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-02-art-streaming-phase2.md:16 and 2026-08-08-art-streaming-phase2-v2.md:44 both state games/sonic4/data/editor/ojz/ is auto-committed by a daemon ~60s after edit — so each aeon save silently commits the obsolete descriptor back into the engine repo. Zero tests in aurora compare act-descriptor.ts against engine/structs.emp; test/export/pipeline.test.ts only checks Aurora's own output against itself.
findings.fix: Either delete the act_descriptor/vram_bases/entity_data emission from saveAeonProject (aeon's recorded direction of travel — DEFERRED_WORK.md:1000 'editor authors JSON, BUILD generates engine format' — Aurora already writes the editor-native section_N.tiles.bin/chunks.json that ojz_strip_gen.py consumes), or regenerate act-descriptor.ts from engine/structs.emp and add a test that fails when Act/Sec field order or sizeof drifts.

verdict.reasoning:
I independently traced the defect end to end and it is factually real, but the severity framing does not survive.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (concrete trigger): open the OJZ aeon project in Aurora (actConfig.dataPath = games/sonic4/data/editor/ojz/act1/) and press Save. saveAeonProject (src/renderer/state/aeon-save.ts:25) -> buildAeonSavePlan (src/core/project/aeon/save.ts:222 exportAct) -> src/core/export/index.ts:71 generateActDescriptorAsm -> src/core/export/act-descriptor.ts.

Layout divergence verified by hand-counting emitted directives against the engine struct:
- Aurora Act = 4+2+2+2+2+1+1+(2*4)+4+4+4 = 34 bytes, with the cam_min_x/cam_max_x/cam_min_y/cam_max_y block at act-descriptor.ts:34-37. aeon/engine/structs.emp:26-51 declares Act = 40 bytes ($28) with NO cam block; act_bg_layout sits at $0E exactly where Aurora writes cam_min_x, and the engine added act_art_pool_table($1A), act_art_pool_pages($1E), edge_mode($20), pad_21($21), act_sec_local_maps($22), act_art_budget($26) — none emitted.
- Aurora Sec = 14 dc.l (56) + 2 dc.w (4) + 4 dc.b (4) + dc.l (4) + 2 dc.w (4) = 72 bytes, padding nulls `dcb.b 72, 0` (act-descriptor.ts:59). structs.emp:107-132 declares Sec = 66 ($42). Field renames confirmed: Aurora sec_reserved_2C(:77) is the engine's sec_block_dict($2C); Aurora sec_collision_s4lz(:79) is now sec_effects($34); sec_camera_lookahead($3D) and sec_block_dict_len($40) are never emitted.
- Directory resurrection confirmed: games/sonic4/data/editor/ojz/act1/export/{act_descriptor.asm,entity_data.asm,section_N.*.bin} present with 2026-08-12 timestamps, post-dating commit 46c2e0f (2026-08-01, "Parcel J: delete the parked ojz editor exports").
- Test gap confirmed and worse than stated: test/export/act-descriptor.test.ts:60-72 affirmatively asserts `dcb.b 72, 0`, locking the wrong Sec size into the suite. Nothing compares against structs.emp.

WHAT BROKE (why severity is wrong, not the facts):
1. No consumer. aeon/build.sh:79 sets MAIN_ASM="games/sonic4/game_root.asm"; grep for "editor" in game_root.asm returns nothing, and games/sonic4/map.toml has zero ".asm" matches. The engine's live descriptor is games/sonic4/data/levels/ojz/act1/act_descriptor.emp — different directory, different extension, and a TYPED Act literal (its own header: "field-order drift cannot compile"). Aurora's .asm cannot be included, cannot overwrite the .emp, and cannot reach the ROM. The only build-graph grep hit for "act1/export" was a self-match inside Aurora's own emitted comment.
2. The "silently commits the obsolete descriptor back into the engine repo" link is not just unproven, it is contradicted by the current state: `git status` shows `?? games/sonic4/data/editor/ojz/act1/export/`, `git ls-files` on that path is EMPTY, and `git check-ignore` returns rc=1 (not ignored) — i.e. untracked and uncommitted four days after the 2026-08-12 write. No auto-commit process is running (`ps aux | grep commit` empty) and .git/hooks has no non-sample hooks. The daemon claim rests on plan-doc prose, not observed behavior.
3. No user work is lost or corrupted. The editor-native artifact ojz_strip_gen.py actually consumes is ${dataPath}section_N.tiles.bin (save.ts:66-70); the remapped export twin lands in ${dataPath}export/section_N.tiles.bin (save.ts:242). Different directories — no clobber of authored data. Also, the export block is wrapped in try/catch (save.ts:221-247) surfacing as a non-fatal exportError, so it cannot even fail a save.
4. The aeon repo's own record grades it exactly this way: DEFERRED_WORK.md strikes the entry through as "VOID 2026-08-05 (the artifact was deleted)", and its surviving historical text says "So it is no build/runtime risk." The finding cites that same file's evidence while dropping its conclusion.

So: the code defect is CONFIRMED (dead exporter emitting a stale, un-assemblable struct layout, plus recreation of a deliberately deleted directory and a test suite that pins the wrong size), but it is not "wrong output or broken main-path feature" — the output is inert and the aeon build is structurally immune.
verdict.severity_correction: Downgrade high -> low. "High" requires wrong output or a broken main-path feature; neither holds. The emitted act_descriptor.asm has no consumer: build.sh:79 roots the residual AS at games/sonic4/game_root.asm (zero "editor" references), map.toml has zero .asm references, and the live descriptor is a typed .emp literal at games/sonic4/data/levels/ojz/act1/act_descriptor.emp that Aurora's file cannot be included by or overwrite. The claimed auto-commit consequence did not occur — the directory is untracked and unignored four days after being written. The main aeon save path (editor-native section_N.tiles.bin, chunks.json, project.json) is untouched, and the export block is try/caught as non-fatal. Residual real harm is limited to: dead code emitting an obsolete artifact, git-status noise plus resurrection of a directory the engine deliberately deleted, and a test suite (test/export/act-descriptor.test.ts:60-72) that actively pins the wrong 72-byte Sec size and would resist a future correct rewrite. That is low — cleanup work, not a bug with a victim. A case for "medium" exists only if one weights the latent trap of the pinning tests plus the directory resurrection; nothing above medium is defensible.

findings.title: FG_TILE_LIMIT = 1024 mirrors an aeon constant that is 896, and check_budget reports fits/limit from it
findings.claim: Aurora's FG tile-pool ceiling is hardcoded at 1024 with a comment justifying it as 'BG region starts at tile slot 1024'; the aeon engine's declared VRAM contract gives fg_art_pool only 896 tiles (slots 896-1023 belong to dust/character/ring/test windows), so the check_budget MCP tool advertises 128 tiles of headroom that do not exist.
findings.evidence: src/core/export/vram-coloring.ts:4-5: `// BG region starts at tile slot 1024 ($400); FG group unions must fit below it.` / `export const FG_TILE_LIMIT = 1024;`, used at :44 to throw 'VRAM overflow' and at src/core/agent/budget.ts:81 as `{ limit: FG_TILE_LIMIT, fits: cursor <= FG_TILE_LIMIT }`, which is what the `check_budget` tool returns (src/renderer/agent/agent-handler.ts:218-231; described in src/main/editor-methods.ts:60 as 'per VRAM color group vs the 1024-tile FG pool. fits=false means export will fail'). Ground truth: aeon/games/sonic4/vram.toml declares region fg_art_pool base=0 tiles=896 with the inline note '960 -> 896: the top page surrendered to the dust', then dust_puff@896(16), dust_spindash@912(12), free@924(36), character_window@960(32), test_obj@992(8), ring_placeholder@1000(16), test_marker@1016(4), free@1020(4), and only then bg_region@1024. aeon/tools/vram_map.py:24 `POOL_TILE_CEILING = 896`; aeon/games/demo/vram.toml carries the same 896 with 'follows the engine-global POOL_TILE_CEILING'. The divergence dates to aeon commit c51a4ff9 (2026-08-11 21:47) 'the dust pool carve'. Not academic: the shipped OJZ act1 export on disk is group0=603 tiles (section_0.art.bin = 19296 B) + group1=281 (section_1.art.bin = 8992 B) = 884 tiles, i.e. 12 tiles under the real 896 ceiling, while Aurora reports 884/1024 and fits=true. Adding ~13 unique tiles to the second colour group makes Aurora answer fits=true for a layout whose group-1 base lands on dust_puff. No downstream catch: aeon/tools/ojz_strip_gen.py:1776 records 'identity-residency guard (OJZ_ACT_POOL_TILES <= POOL_TILE_CEILING) is retired' and :1774 'there is no per-act VRAM fit to guard'. No aurora test references POOL_TILE_CEILING or 896; grep for FG_TILE_LIMIT hits only budget.ts, vram-coloring.ts and test/export/vram-coloring.test.ts (which asserts against the same 1024 literal on both sides).
findings.fix: Stop mirroring: read the ceiling from aeon's declared contract (games/<game>/vram.toml fg_art_pool, or the generated tools/vram_map.py POOL_TILE_CEILING) at project load, and drop 1024 from vram-coloring.ts. If the number must stay hardcoded, add a test that reads aeon's vram.toml when present and fails on inequality. Separately, revisit whether an act-wide union budget is still the right model at all now that the engine pages 64-tile pages (PAGE_TABLE_MAX=256, ojz_strip_gen.py:131).

verdict.reasoning:
I traced every link of the claimed path and the failure scenario breaks at the consumer end.

What is true (and only this): `src/core/export/vram-coloring.ts:5` hardcodes `FG_TILE_LIMIT = 1024`; `src/core/agent/budget.ts:81` returns it as `limit`/`fits`; `src/main/editor-methods.ts:60` describes it as "the 1024-tile FG pool"; and `/home/volence/sonic_hacks/aeon/games/sonic4/vram.toml` really does declare `fg_art_pool base=0 tiles=896` with dust/character/ring windows at 896-1023. The two numbers do differ.

What breaks the finding — the "group-1 base lands on dust_puff" harm requires some consumer to place Aurora's cumulative group bases into VRAM. No such consumer exists:

1. `sec_tile_art_vram` — the field that carried a per-section VRAM base — exists NOWHERE in aeon's engine/, games/ or tools/ any more. `grep -rn sec_tile_art_vram engine/ games/ tools/` returns hits only inside Aurora's own stale artifact `games/sonic4/data/editor/ojz/act1/export/act_descriptor.asm`. The live descriptor is `games/sonic4/data/levels/ojz/act1/act_descriptor.emp` and has no such field.

2. Nothing in aeon reads Aurora's `export/` directory. `build.sh` references no editor/export path; grep for `/export/`, `vram_bases`, `.art.bin` across aeon's .py/.emp/.asm/.sh/.toml finds zero consumers, and the exported `.art.bin`/`.tiles.bin` are gitignored (`aeon/.gitignore:2 *.bin`). What the build actually consumes is `editor/ojz/act1/section_N.tiles.bin` + `editor/ojz/chunks_tiles.bin` (`tools/ojz_strip_gen.py:1590`), which Aurora writes at `src/core/project/aeon/save.ts:70` from the RAW nametable — untouched by `assignVramBases`. The base-remapped copies go to `dataPath/export/` (save.ts:230-242) and are dead output.

3. The engine has no 896-tile per-act fit at all. `tools/ojz_strip_gen.py:1770-1776`: "pages land in ALLOCATED frames (dest = frame base, not page_id*64), so there is no per-act VRAM fit to guard … the old identity-residency guard (OJZ_ACT_POOL_TILES <= POOL_TILE_CEILING) is retired." `POOL_TILE_CEILING` is imported but used at exactly one site, the informational print at :1955 ("ceiling {POOL_TILE_CEILING}"). The real hard cap is `PAGE_TABLE_MAX = 256` pages x 64 tiles (:131). The seat quoted line 1776 and still asserted an 896 hard ceiling. So the concrete trigger it offers ("add ~13 unique tiles to the second colour group and group-1's base lands on dust_puff") produces no overlap, no corrupted art, no wrong ROM — the pool is deduped and paged by ojz_strip_gen from the tileset/nametables, and a 900- or 2000-tile act is legal.

4. The tool's operative promise is internally true. budget.ts computes the union exactly as export does (blank-seed + flip-aware) so `fits === !exportThrows` against `assignVramBases` (vram-coloring.ts:44). "fits=false means export will fail" holds; `npx vitest run test/export/vram-coloring.test.ts test/agent/budget.test.ts` passes 10/10.

The 884-vs-896 "12 tiles of headroom" narrative is also inert: those byte counts come from the gitignored export/ blobs, not from the shipped ROM art, which ojz_strip_gen derives independently.

Residual, much smaller issue: 1024 is a stale legacy constant that matches neither aeon's declared fg_art_pool (896) nor the engine's actual paged cap, and `check_budget`'s description narrates it as an engine VRAM fact. That is doc/model staleness in an advisory tool plus dead export output — worth cleaning up, not a defect that produces wrong output.
verdict.severity_correction: If retained at all, low (stale advisory constant / dead export artifact), not high. High requires wrong output or a broken main path; the only artifact affected by FG_TILE_LIMIT is aurora's export/ directory, which no aeon build step reads, and the engine imposes no per-act VRAM tile ceiling for the value to be wrong against.

findings.title: BG_MAX_TILES = 512 is the last unreconciled copy of a constant aeon fixed to 448 in 2026-06
findings.claim: The set_bg tool accepts up to 512 BG tiles; aeon's BG region is 448 tiles ($8000-$B7FF, bounded by the relocated sprite attribute table), and aeon explicitly finished reconciling every other copy of that number away from 512 on 2026-06-23.
findings.evidence: src/renderer/agent/agent-handler.ts:44 `const BG_MAX_TILES = 512;` enforced at :455; src/main/editor-methods.ts:96 schema `.min(1).max(512)`, with the tool descriptions at :94 and :97 both telling agents 'max 512 tiles'. Ground truth: aeon/tools/vram_map.py:26 `BG_TILE_CAPACITY = 448`; aeon/games/sonic4/vram.toml bg_region base=1024 tiles=448; aeon/games/sonic4/config/constants.emp:317 and games/demo/config/constants.emp:50 both `ensure(BG_TILE_CAPACITY == 448, ...)`; aeon/engine/level/bg.emp:48-51 computes BG_TILE_REGION_BYTES = VRAM_SPRITE_TABLE - BG_TILE_BASE_VRAM = $3800 = 448 tiles and calls 512 'the stale BG_TILE_CAPACITY=512 nominal'. aeon/docs/DEFERRED_WORK.md:983-986 is a RESOLVED entry titled 'BG_TILE_CAPACITY reconciliation (512 -> 448)' listing every site fixed (constants.asm, ojz_strip_gen.py, inject_editor_bg.py) — Aurora is not on that list and still says 512. aeon/tools/inject_editor_bg.py:18-24 imports the value from one authority and its comment names 'the four-copies-of-448 incident'; :133 `assert len(tiles) <= BG_TILE_CAPACITY`. Concrete failure: an agent calls set_bg with 480 tiles; Aurora accepts it, stores it, reports success, the user saves, and the aeon build then dies on that assert with no trace back to the tool that produced it. The live override file games/sonic4/data/editor_bg_override.json already carries exactly 448 tiles, i.e. zero real headroom. No aurora test references 448.
findings.fix: Change BG_MAX_TILES and the set_bg zod max to 448 and correct both tool descriptions; better, derive it from the project's vram.toml when the aeon project supplies one.

findings.title: The /mcp endpoint has no Host/Origin validation while /aether does, and the installed MCP SDK provides none by default
findings.claim: protocol.md D8 makes the loopback Origin/Host check Aurora's responsibility; it is applied to /aether and /aether/events but not to /mcp, which serves the same 33 editing tools (including open_project and save_project) with no header validation from Aurora or from the SDK.
findings.evidence: src/main/mcp-server.ts:65 `exp.post('/mcp', async (req,res) => {...})` — no middleware. The loopbackOnly middleware defined at :83-91 is applied only at :97 (`exp.post('/aether', loopbackOnly, ...)`) and :107 (`exp.get('/aether/events', loopbackOnly, ...)`). The comment at :81-82 states the trust model ('loopback bind + Origin/Host check, never remotely exposed (protocol D8)') beside the endpoint that has it, not the one that doesn't. The SDK is constructed as `new StreamableHTTPServerTransport({ sessionIdGenerator: undefined })` (:68) with no allowedHosts/allowedOrigins/enableDnsRebindingProtection. Verified in the installed SDK (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.29.0): dist/esm/server/streamableHttp.js contains no occurrence of 'host', 'origin' or 'DnsRebinding' at all (it delegates to webStandardStreamableHttp.js), and dist/esm/server/sse.js:22 shows the family default `this._options = options || { enableDnsRebindingProtection: false }` — protection is opt-in and Aurora does not opt in. Aurora also builds its express app by hand rather than via the SDK's createMcpExpressApp (dist/esm/server/express.js:27-32), which is where hostHeaderValidation would have been wired. Failure scenario: a page served from http://attacker.example:38473/ whose DNS then rebinds to 127.0.0.1 makes same-origin fetches to /mcp (no CORS preflight, no Host check) and can call open_project on an arbitrary path plus every classic mutation tool and save_project against the user's disasm. No test in test/main covers mcp-server.ts at all — aether-adapter.test.ts tests the adapter function, never the express wiring, so loopbackOnly itself is also never exercised.
findings.fix: Apply `loopbackOnly` to `exp.post('/mcp')` (and the 405 handlers) exactly as /aether does, or pass `{ enableDnsRebindingProtection: true, allowedHosts: ['127.0.0.1:'+port, 'localhost:'+port] }` to StreamableHTTPServerTransport. Add a test that POSTs with `Host: evil.example` and asserts 403 — today no such test exists for either endpoint.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED — I tried to break the chain at four points (a missed global guard, SDK-side defaults, CORS, and the MCP initialize handshake) and all four held. I then reproduced the exploit against a live server.

**1. The asymmetry is real (read at pinned SHA 2b38e0b).** /home/volence/sonic_hacks/aurora/src/main/mcp-server.ts:65 `exp.post('/mcp', async (req, res) => {...})` takes no middleware; :77 and :78 (the 405 handlers) likewise. `loopbackOnly` is defined at :83-91 and applied only at :97 (`/aether`) and :107 (`/aether/events`). The only app-wide middleware is `exp.use(express.json({limit:'16mb'}))` at :62 — I grepped all of src/main for `cors|helmet|Access-Control` and got zero hits. `startMcpServer` is called unconditionally at src/main/index.ts:64 (no dev-only gate).

**2. The SDK provides nothing — verified in the installed tree, not from memory.** node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk is version 1.29.0. `dist/esm/server/streamableHttp.js` is a thin wrapper that passes `options` straight to `WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport`; `dist/esm/server/webStandardStreamableHttp.js:70` is the authoritative default: `this._enableDnsRebindingProtection = options.enableDnsRebindingProtection ?? false`. The Host/Origin validator at :104-127 is entirely gated behind `if (!this._enableDnsRebindingProtection) return;` at :109. Aurora constructs `new StreamableHTTPServerTransport({ sessionIdGenerator: undefined })` (:68) — no allowedHosts, no allowedOrigins, no opt-in. (Minor correction to the seat's evidence: the load-bearing line is webStandardStreamableHttp.js:70, not sse.js:22.) Aurora also hand-builds express rather than using `createMcpExpressApp` (dist/esm/server/express.js:27-38), which is the only place `localhostHostValidation()` gets wired.

**3. The initialize handshake does NOT gate it — this is worse than the seat claimed.** I expected to refute here, since Aurora builds a *fresh* McpServer+transport per POST (:67-68), so no session state survives a request. But webStandardStreamableHttp.js `validateSession` returns `undefined` immediately when `sessionIdGenerator === undefined` (stateless mode), short-circuiting the `if (!this._initialized) reject all requests` check just below it. So a single POST containing only `tools/call`, with no initialize, no Mcp-Session-Id and no Mcp-Protocol-Version, reaches the tool handler.

**4. Reproduced.** I stood up a standalone server replicating mcp-server.ts:65-76 verbatim (scratchpad/rebind.mjs, outside the repo — no files modified) with an `open_project` tool. One POST with `Host: attacker.example:38999`, `Origin: http://attacker.example:38999`, no handshake:
`status=200`, `body={"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"opened /home/victim/secret-disasm"}]}}`, `TOOL RAN WITH: {"path":"/home/victim/secret-disasm"}`.
And the guard Aurora already owns would have stopped exactly that request: `/^(127\.0\.0\.1|localhost|\[::1\]|::1)(:\d+)?$/i.test('attacker.example:38999')` → **false** → 403. Applied to `/aether`, not to `/mcp`.

**Concrete trigger:** attacker serves a page on `http://attacker.example:38473/` with a short-TTL A record, rebinds it to 127.0.0.1, then `fetch('/mcp', {method:'POST', headers:{'content-type':'application/json','accept':'application/json, text/event-stream'}, body: <tools/call open_project>})`. It is same-origin post-rebind, so no preflight; the browser sends `Host: attacker.example:38473`, which Aurora never inspects. All 33 EDITOR_METHODS (confirmed count; `open_project` at editor-methods.ts:108, `save_project` at :155) are reachable.

**Two honest caveats that narrow but do not refute it.** (a) A plain non-rebinding cross-origin POST from evil.com *is* blocked: the transport requires `Content-Type: application/json` (webStandardStreamableHttp.js:382-385), which forces a CORS preflight that Aurora answers without `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. So DNS rebinding is genuinely required — the loopback bind at :118 does block the naive remote path. (b) Chrome's Private Network Access may interfere in some configurations, but that is a browser-side mitigation, absent in Firefox/Safari, and not a code-side guard.

Seat's test claim also verified: `grep -rln "mcp-server" test/` returns nothing — mcp-server.ts has no coverage, so `loopbackOnly` itself is never exercised either.

findings.title: The Aether initialize result omits two schema-REQUIRED keys, and no reply carries the required envelope fields
findings.claim: capabilities() returns none of timingBasis, limits, frame, mclk, running or droppedEvents, all of which empyrean/contract/schema/bus-protocol.schema.json marks required on the initialize result, and no success/error reply carries the machine stamp or dropped-event counter that §2.2/§2.3 make envelope-level and §8 item 10 applies to 'any conformant server'.
findings.evidence: src/main/aether/adapter.ts:31-39 returns exactly `{serverName, serverVersion, protocolVersion, capabilities:{events, editorMethods}, methods}`. empyrean/contract/schema/bus-protocol.schema.json `handshake.initialize.result` has `required: [serverName, protocolVersion, capabilities, methods, timingBasis, limits]` plus `allOf: [{$ref:'#/$defs/replyFields'}]`, and replyFields is `allOf:[stamp] + required:[droppedEvents]` where stamp is `required:[frame,mclk,running]`. `$defs/successResponse` puts result: replyFields, so EVERY editor/* success reply is non-conformant too — src/main/aether/protocol.ts:44 `ok = (id,result) => ({jsonrpc:'2.0',id,result})` applies nothing, and :45 `err` builds error.data only when a caller passes it, so error.data is absent on -32601/-32603 where the schema says it is 'always present'. protocol.md §7.2 explicitly calls this adapter 'conformant, not a second protocol — it carries the identical envelope', and §8's post-amendment list is prefaced 'these apply to any conformant server, not only the original C++ one'. test/main/aether-adapter.test.ts asserts only protocolVersion/serverName/methods/events (lines 15-19) — it cannot fail on any of the missing keys. Note the contract itself is emulator-shaped here (frame/mclk/running/maxRunFrames have no editor meaning), so this may be a contract gap rather than an Aurora bug — but today Aurora's adapter would fail schema validation against the published schema and nothing detects that.
findings.fix: Either (a) raise it with the contract owner and get an editor-role exemption written into §2.2/§2.1, or (b) emit the fields structurally in ok()/err() (frame/mclk = 0, running = false, droppedEvents from a per-connection counter) and add timingBasis + limits (maxReadLen matching get_tiles' 256 cap, maxLineBytes matching the 16mb express.json limit) to capabilities(). Either way add a test that validates capabilities() against contract/schema/bus-protocol.schema.json so the answer is enforced rather than asserted in prose.

findings.title: The SSE channel pushes editor/ready before any initialize/initialized, and broadcast() — the only stamped-event path — is dead code
findings.claim: protocol.md §2.1 and §8 item 3 require a server to reject/withhold events before the client's `initialized` notification; Aurora's /aether/events handler has no session state and writes an editor/ready notification the instant a socket connects, with no machine stamp in its params.
findings.evidence: src/main/mcp-server.ts:107-113: the GET handler sets SSE headers, calls addSubscriber(res), then immediately `res.write('data: ' + JSON.stringify({jsonrpc:'2.0', method:'editor/ready', params:{serverName:'aurora'}}))`. Nothing anywhere tracks whether that connection (or any connection) has sent `initialize`/`initialized` — the POST binding is stateless per-request (:65-76 builds a fresh server+transport per POST; :97 dispatches /aether with no session), and adapter.ts:61 handles `initialized` by returning null and recording nothing. Concrete input: `curl -N http://127.0.0.1:38473/aether/events` with no prior initialize returns an event immediately, which protocol.md §2.1 ('The server MUST NOT push events before initialized') forbids. The params also carry no frame/mclk/running, which §2.2 requires on 'every pushed event'. Separately, adapter.ts:94-99 `broadcast()` is exported and has zero callers in src (grep for broadcast/addSubscriber outside src/main/aether/ hits only mcp-server.ts's import), so `capabilities.events: ['editor/ready']` (adapter.ts:28,36) advertises an event stream whose only emission is the hand-inlined greeting above — the adapter's own event API is never used. test/main/aether-adapter.test.ts covers neither.
findings.fix: Give the SSE endpoint a handshake gate (a session id from initialize, or at minimum refuse the stream until an initialized has been seen), route the greeting through broadcast() so one code path stamps events, and either use broadcast() for real editor events or drop editor/ready from capabilities.events.

findings.title: get_bg hardcodes height 32 while list_bgs derives it, so the documented get_bg→set_bg round-trip breaks on any non-32-row background
findings.claim: get_bg reports `height: BG_TILES_HIGH` (a constant 32) while returning the whole bgLayout array, list_bgs computes height as bgLayout.length/64, and set_bg accepts exactly 2048 words — three different answers to the same question, and the engine's Plane B is 64x64 with all 64 rows live.
findings.evidence: src/renderer/agent/agent-handler.ts:43 `const BG_TILES_HIGH = 32;`, used at :446 as get_bg's declared height while :448 returns `Array.from(ctx.act.bgLayout)` unconditionally; :535 list_bgs instead reports `height: Math.floor(ctx.act.bgLayout.length / BG_WIDTH)`; :464 set_bg rejects anything but `BG_WIDTH * BG_TILES_HIGH` = 2048 words, and src/main/editor-methods.ts:96 pins the schema at `.length(2048)` while :94 promises 'a get_bg result can be fed straight back to set_bg'. src/core/formats/bg-tiles.ts:37 documents BG_WIDTH as 'the engine's fixed 64x32 Plane B'; aeon/engine/level/bg.emp:15-34 says the layout is 'a raw 64x64 = 8192 bytes (full Plane B nametable)' and 'ALL 64 ROWS ARE LIVE (NEW-5 close, 2026-08-05) … the shipped OJZ override carries real art in rows 32-63, and the full-plane vscroll wrap … puts those rows on screen, including at spawn'. aeon/tools/inject_editor_bg.py:130-132 accepts 2048 OR 4096 words ('legacy 32-row layout: pad to 64 rows'), and the live games/sonic4/data/editor_bg_override.json I measured has layout length 4096. Failure scenario: point Aurora at any act whose bgLayout binary is the 64-row shape (4096 words) — get_bg returns 4096 entries labelled height 32, list_bgs labels the same act height 64, and feeding get_bg's output to set_bg errors 'layout must have 2048 words'. Today aeon's ojz_act1_bg.bin is 4096 bytes = 2048 words so it does not bite, but nothing prevents it and no test covers the disagreement.
findings.fix: Derive height from `bgLayout.length / BG_WIDTH` in get_bg the way list_bgs already does, and let set_bg accept 2048 or 4096 words (matching inject_editor_bg.py's own rule) rather than a fixed length. Fix the bg-tiles.ts:37 comment — the engine's Plane B is 64x64.

findings.title: The MCP discovery file restates protocolVersion as a literal instead of importing PROTOCOL_VERSION
findings.claim: ~/.aurora/mcp.json (and the legacy ~/.sonic-level-editor/mcp.json) writes `protocolVersion: 1` as a hand-typed literal while the adapter answers initialize from src/main/aether/protocol.ts's PROTOCOL_VERSION, so a version bump makes the two disagree silently.
findings.evidence: src/main/mcp-server.ts:134-141 builds the discovery JSON with `protocolVersion: 1` even though the module already imports from './aether/adapter'; src/main/aether/protocol.ts:8 `export const PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1` is what adapter.ts:35 reports and what adapter.ts:56 negotiates against with -32015. Concrete input: change protocol.ts:8 to 2 — initialize then answers 2 and rejects clients sending 1, while mcp.json still advertises 1, so a discovery-driven client negotiates the version it was told and is refused. Nothing reads mcp.json in any test (no test/main file references it), so the divergence is invisible until a client fails. Same shape at a smaller scale: SERVER_VERSION '0.1.0' is written twice (src/main/aether/adapter.ts:22 and mcp-server.ts:19) and neither reads package.json's version field (currently also 0.1.0, so not yet diverged).
findings.fix: Import PROTOCOL_VERSION into mcp-server.ts and use it in the discovery payload; likewise hoist the server version to one constant sourced from package.json.

findings.title: Oracle integration is an approved but wholly unimplemented contract — no emulator client exists in Aurora
findings.claim: Aurora's approved Aether-client playtest design specifies an emulator/* client (method calls, event subscription, symbol resolution, a build→load_symbols→reload_rom loop); there is no implementation anywhere in src, so this is a dormant contract with nothing to drift against yet.
findings.evidence: docs/specs/2026-07-03-aether-client-playtest-design.md:33-70 specifies `emulator/<name>` calls, subscription to `emulator/stopped`/`emulator/resumed`/`emulator/romReloaded` forwarded to the renderer over IPC, `emulator/lookup_symbol` resolution after every connect, throttled `emulator/write_cram` on slider drag, and on build exit 0 `emulator/load_symbols` then `emulator/reload_rom`. A grep of src for 'emulator/' or 'oracle' returns only unrelated uses of the word 'oracle' as a test-fixture term (src/renderer/components/art-shared/zoom-anchor.ts:51, __tests__/zoom-cap.test.ts:19, __tests__/zoom-anchor.test.ts:22,104, src/renderer/state/classicLevelStore.ts:275). Aurora is exclusively an Aether *server* today (src/main/aether/), never a client. The one thing worth recording as non-drift: empyrean/contract/protocol.md §10 decision 4 / §11.1 CR-6 record that this very spec once subscribed to `emulator/rom_reloaded` and was corrected; the spec at :35 now reads `emulator/romReloaded`, matching the contract.
findings.fix: No code fix. Flag in the roadmap that the spec is unimplemented so nobody treats it as a shipped capability, and re-verify its method/event names against protocol.md §6 before building (the catalog has moved substantially — §11.1 through §11.11 amendments run to 2026-08-16).
